## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.kt

## Trigger

`RaceLaunchController.openPreparation`, called from `PreparationViewModel`'s
init block on the first reference-race emission — observed. The `opened`
flag guards only against a second call within the same ViewModel instance;
on a new instance it defaults to false, so `openPreparation` — and its
`findInProgress()` call — always runs after process death, as it should.

## Today

`RaceLaunchController.openPreparation` calls `recordingRepository.findInProgress()`
and, when it returns a race, returns `PreparationState.Resuming` — which
`PreparationViewModel.applyState` already handles by navigating straight to
the race screen (`navigator.launchRace()`), with no screen of its own. This
resume path is wired correctly.

The defect is in `RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl` itself: it keeps every race
in a plain `LinkedHashMap<Long, Race>` held in the instance
(`private val races = LinkedHashMap<Long, Race>()`), with the class comment
stating it "holds every race it opens for the lifetime of this instance".
Nothing writes a race, or its segment progress, to Room. After a process
death the new instance's map is empty, so `findInProgress()` always returns
`null` — `openPreparation` then falls through to `openSession()` and opens
a fresh preparation, exactly as the gap describes, but the cause is the
repository's in-memory storage, not the `opened` flag.

The watch already has a Room-backed `RaceDao` (`core-data`), injected as
`RaceRepository` for the reference race and history — `app-wear`'s
`RepositoryModule` builds a real `HyroxDatabase` and provides `RaceDao`.
`RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl` does not use it: it is constructed with only
`ProfileRepository` and never touches `RaceDao`.

## Expected

`RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl` persists the race it is recording — its row
and current-segment state — to the database as it opens the clock and marks
each segment, so `findInProgress()` reads that state back after a process
death and correctly returns the in-progress race, letting
`openPreparation` return `PreparationState.Resuming` as designed.

Second gap: `RaceDao` (core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/db/RaceDao.kt)
carries no query to find a race with an open segment. `findInProgress`
needs one — e.g. `SELECT * FROM races WHERE currentSegmentIndex IS NOT NULL
LIMIT 1` — since the existing queries (`observeAll`, `observeReference`,
`findById`, `findBySourceRaceId`) do not select on that condition.
